problem: Consider the equation ${y}^{″}-2{y}^{′}-15y=0$ where $y=y(t).$ If $y={e}^{\lambda t}$ is a solution, then $\lambda =$
worked_solution:
Assuming $y={e}^{\lambda t}$ and differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda t},\,{y}^{″}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda t}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda t}-2\lambda {e}^{\lambda t}-15{e}^{\lambda t} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda t}({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -15) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -15 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Factoring the auxiliary equation results in

$$
(\lambda +3)(\lambda -5)=0,
$$

and so the solutions of the auxiliary equation  are $\lambda =-3$ or $\lambda =5.$
